title: Usage errors shift upstream to event-level controls
previous_assumption: Billing leakage can be tested primarily at invoice or revenue-report level.
changed_assumption: Usage-based models require event-level ingestion, idempotency, rejection, and latency checks before invoice and revenue testing.
model_update: Increase weighting for usage-event completeness and rejected-event queues in billing leakage scenarios.

title: Pricing complexity requires billing architecture fit tests
previous_assumption: Billing-system readiness can be scored from invoice output and standard subscription configuration.
changed_assumption: Composite pricing, dimensions, prepaid credits, enterprise contracts, and real-time metering require architecture-specific readiness checks.
model_update: Add pricing complexity and billing primitive fit to S2/S4 heatmap criteria.

title: E-invoicing readiness moves earlier in the handover lifecycle
previous_assumption: VAT and e-invoicing issues can be reviewed after core billing design.
changed_assumption: Structured e-invoice fields, timing, and reporting data should be tested before billing process stabilization for relevant jurisdictions.
model_update: Add jurisdictional e-invoice field completeness and transaction reporting readiness to Step 8.

title: Payment controls split between card environment and ACH operations
previous_assumption: Payment-control maturity can be represented as a single billing operations row.
changed_assumption: Cardholder-data environment controls and ACH fraud monitoring rules require distinct risk rows and evidence artifacts.
model_update: Split payment operations into card-data impact, ACH fraud monitoring, descriptor rules, and return handling.

title: Audit evidence packaging becomes a product requirement
previous_assumption: Evidence support can be assembled during audit or diligence request response.
changed_assumption: High-risk handover outputs should include audit-ready evidence lineage, retained source references, and reviewer signoff from the start.
model_update: Increase weighting for evidence lineage, retained-source mapping, and reviewer trail in S3/S4.

title: Internal segment transaction pressure is a standalone leakage scenario
previous_assumption: Segment-reporting risk is mostly downstream financial reporting review.
changed_assumption: Unsupported intersegment pricing, rebates, and performance adjustments can originate in operating-model pressure and should be treated as a handover scenario.
model_update: Add intersegment pricing pressure transfer to reporting and disclosure-control heatmap dimensions.
